slo_title: Apply the Self Referential Structure and Structure Pointer

mcq.q: If struct Node is a self-referential structure with a pointer to itself, what is the output of the following code? struct Node { int data; struct Node *next; }; int main() { struct Node n1, n2; n1.data = 10; n2.data = 20; n1.next = &n2; printf("%d", n1.next->data); return 0; }

What is the result of the following code snippet? struct Point { int x; int y; }; struct Point* createPoint(int x, int y) { struct Point *p = (struct Point*)malloc(sizeof(struct Point)); p->x = x; p->y = y; return p; }

options.A: The code creates a structure and initializes it with x and y values, but it does not allocate memory.
options.B: The code dynamically allocates memory for a Point structure and initializes its members
options.C: The code results in a compile-time error due to incorrect memory allocation.
options.D: The code will result in a runtime error if malloc fails

mcq.answer_text: The code dynamically allocates memory for a Point structure and initializes its members

sq.q: Write a C program to define a structure for storing student information (name, roll number, and Branch. Use a pointer to a structure to access and display the student details. Include appropriate input and output operations
answer: The structure pointer points to the address of a memory block where the Structure is being stored.
Structure pointer tells the address of a structure in memory by pointing pointer variable ptr to the structure variable.
pointer ptr is pointing to the address structure_variable of the Structure
